author: twinkie_d

item.authorHandle: twinkie_d
item.caption:
I got my vote on today! 
It was nice and quiet when I got here.  No lines and it WAS QUIET. 
Then some asshat came in with his (elementary?) son.  The dad was talking a bit loudly and kept saying “yes”, “no”, or “we don’t like them”…etc. 

I was at the tail end of voting and then reviewing my votes and all the chatter was throwing me off. I had made a feeble attempt to use the headphone provided but it didn’t work. 
I asked if I could move to a different booth since he was so distracting. 
The staff was saying that I would need start all over again. 🙄🙄🙄 

I audible complained out him, he was just telling me under his breath to “just focus”. 
WTF‽ 🤬🤬🤬 Thank god I double and triple checked my ballot.  Some were mis-marked! 

I looked through my bag and found my headphones and played music to drown the asshat who was still saying what votes he was casting. 

I’m kinda surprised the people that work here didn’t tell him to keep his votes to himself. 

Buuuuuuuuuuttttttt, I finally got my votes in. 
Can’t wait for the election in two years to finally get competent people running our country. 
 
#IVoted
#YourVoiceMatters
#GrabEmByTheBallot

author: victsim

item.authorHandle: victsim
item.caption:
I made my voice heard and voted!

And leadership was at the center of every choice I made.

I’ve spent my career holding leaders accountable for how they treat people, how they make decisions, and the results they deliver. I expect the same from those asking to lead our communities, our states, and our country.

I’m tired of the political theater, the lies, the fearmongering, the racism, the bigotry, the grifting & corruption and the blind loyalty that puts party above principle and political power above people.

Enough already!

My father served four United States presidents. Two from one side of the isle and the other two from the other side. I grew up understanding that public service is a responsibility and an honor. It demands integrity, character, courage, and a commitment to something greater than yourself. I saw it first hand in my family and had numerous conversations with President Ford. We would talk about whatever sport I was playing at the time, how I was doing in school and how was my mom and sisters doing. While I saw him in an informal setting he was always friendly, open and presidential. When my dad retired we held a party at La Quinta Hotel and he came to the dinner with Mrs. Ford and when he took the stage he talked about how appreciative he was of my father and the work he did and his years of service in the Air Force and before he left the stage he talked about Mrs. Ford and glowed her up with accolades first and then talked about how she too appreciated my dad and then talked about me, my mom and my sisters never once making the evening about him. 

We can disagree on policy. We can debate how best to move this country forward. But I will NEVER accept racism, bigotry, dishonesty, or the deliberate division of people as acceptable forms of leadership.

Character matters. Integrity matters. Accountability matters. And the greater good matters.

The title may get you into office, but it doesn’t make you a leader.

I cast my vote accordingly.

#IVoted #Leadership #Accountability #Democracy #LeadWithPresence
